text: Cream standardised to 18 % fat and pasteurised, not homogenised unless sold as extra-thick. Too lean to whip, it is poured.

links.name: Wikipedia: Cream (UK grades, Food Labelling Regulations 1996)

sources.text: The table, the facts and the words on how it is made, from these.

steps.note: Single cream is set to 18 % fat, too lean to whip.
At this fat the handbook's coffee-cream heating of 85 to 95 °C for up to 15 to 20 seconds applies.
It is cooled to about 5 °C straight after heating.

links.name: Tetra Pak Dairy Processing Handbook, ch. 9 Pasteurized and ESL dairy products

sources.text: The handbook for heating and cooling of cream of 10 to 18 % fat; Wikipedia for the UK 18 % grade, which is not sterilised. The handbook's step of homogenising is left out because plain single cream is not homogenised.
